correctness.rationale: Every square-zero endomorphism is uniquely an image–kernel flag plus a quotient-to-image isomorphism. Given X, the two prescribed product ranks are intersections of im Y with ker X and im X with ker Y, respectively. Nested Gaussian subspace counts with independent graph-of-map lifts yield the exact finite sum. Nonempty summation bounds are equivalent to |r-s| <= n-a-b, and a separate Grassmannian incidence argument yields the balanced formula. Normalization and symmetry follow from the bijection; direct small-field exhaustive tests, including GF(4), corroborate but do not prove the unrestricted symbolic statement.

value.rationale: The four-rank counting function is a canonical and complete finite-field arithmetic invariant for representations of the algebra with two square-zero generators and no mixed relation. It records directional asymmetry, proves a sharp bidirectional rank obstruction with realizability, and has a nontrivial diagonal degeneration when both operators have maximal square-zero rank. These are intrinsic structural and enumerative properties, not arbitrary parameter slices; an earlier equivalent incidence formula remains a value-independent priority risk.
